title: What Is Done: The Se Construction

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know the passive *se* from B1 Unit 6: *se* + a verb in the third person, when who does it is not important. The verb agrees with the thing: *se vende una arepa*, *se venden arepas*. Laws, markets and neighbourhoods are described this way, which is why it suits a lesson on living together in the city.

items.spanish: Se venden arepas venezolanas en muchas ciudades.
items.english: Venezuelan arepas are sold in many cities.

items.spanish: En Brasil se aprobó una nueva ley de migración en 2017.
items.english: A new migration law was approved in Brazil in 2017.

items.spanish: En Argentina se reconoce la migración como un derecho.
items.english: In Argentina migration is recognised as a right.

items.spanish: En el barrio se celebran fiestas de varios países.
items.english: In the neighbourhood festivals from several countries are celebrated.

sections.content: With a plural thing, the verb is plural too: *se venden arepas*, not *se vende arepas*. The *se* sentence names the thing, not the person who does it.
